products.name: What to Expect When You're Expecting

reviews.content: I bought this book as soon as I found out I was pregnant. Thus far, I've read through the chapter on the 3rd month of pregnancy and everything is great. It's well written, funny, and I'm learning from it. I don't plan on finishing yet, mainly becasue I want to read trimester by trimester, but I have learned from it. There's plenty of information on what to expect with your body changes, the baby's growth, ""side effects"" advice on how to deal with morning sickness, and more! If I have any friends get pregnant in the future, I am going to advise they read this.
reviews.title: Fun, Entertaining and Educatonal!

reviews.content: I bought this for my daughter who is expecting her first child. It has a lot of great information, and she reads it daily. I also bought this book as well as the ""First year"" and ""Toddler years"" books by the same author for my other daughter who just loved them all. I would highly recommend them for any new mother!

reviews.content: I ordered two different books on pregnancy after finding out I am expecting my first baby. I have never been pregnant before and this book gives me all the information I need. My husband and I have been reading it every week for more than 5 months now. I never even refer to the other book I ordered any more. It answers all my questions and is a great resource, especially for first time moms!

reviews.content: This book kept me from calling my doctor every day of my first pregnancy, and I bought a new copy for this one. I gave the old one to a friend who kept calling me and asking medical questions! I also have the ""First Year,"" which really helped defend my decision to breastfeed, and ""Toddler Years"" which helps me keep an eye on my daughter's development. I think this book is a great choice, unless you happen to be an obstetrician. The question and answer format is more informational than sentimental, and there is not room to write about the pregnancy, but you would probably want that in a keepsake book anyway.
reviews.title: For the most paranoia a woman will ever experience. . .
